instructions: Put the rice in a fine strainer and rinse it under cold water. Transfer it to a medium saucepan with 2 1/4 cups water and a pinch of salt. Bring it to a boil, cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on for 5 minutes, then fluff it with a fork.
Peel the squash, scoop out the seeds and cut the flesh into 3/4 inch cubes. That should be about 5 cups. Slit the green chili lengthwise and grate the ginger.
Heat the oil in a large deep skillet over medium heat. Add the bay leaf, cumin seeds, fenugreek seeds and asafoetida. After about 20 seconds the seeds will sizzle and smell toasty.
Add the chili and ginger and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the squash and stir for 2 minutes, until every piece is coated in oil.
Add the turmeric, chili powder, coriander, garam masala and salt. Stir for 2 minutes.
Add 1/3 cup water and cover. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the squash is tender when you pierce it with a fork.

Add the jaggery, the amchur and another 1/3 cup water. Stir gently and cook for 3 minutes, until the squash has taken on the flavors and most of the water is gone. Press a few pieces against the side of the pan to thicken it.
Take the pan off the heat. Chop 3 tbsp of the cilantro and stir it in.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Hebbar's Kitchen (the lead, 5 from 261) sautes whole spices, adds the pumpkin and ground spices, steams it in a little water and finishes with jaggery and amchur for the sweet and sour note. Swasthi's version is similar but uses onion and tomato and no sweetener; Nisha Madhulika's adds mustard oil, a tomato paste and sugar. This version follows the lead, with butternut squash standing in for pumpkin because it peels and cooks faster, and the green chili cut to 1. Rice replaces the poori or roti so it stays gluten-free.
